title: Alabama Business Privilege Tax return and annual report
finding: The blanket filing requirement is wrong. From tax years after December 31, 2023, calculated Business Privilege Tax of $100 or less is exempt from both tax and return filing. Corporate Secretary of State annual reports are separate. Rework entity/form scope and dates before seeding.
originalDescription: Every corporation and LLC organized, registered or doing business in Alabama files a Business Privilege Tax return and annual report with the Department of Revenue, due on the same date as its federal income tax return — Form PPT for LLCs and S corporations, Form CPT for C corporations. It stays due every year until the entity is formally dissolved or withdrawn, active or not. Since 2024 a corporation files its Secretary of State annual report separately.
correctedDraftDescription: For tax years beginning after December 31, 2023, taxpayers whose calculated Alabama Business Privilege Tax is $100 or less are exempt from both the tax and the return-filing requirement. Check the Department of Revenue instructions for your entity's filing obligation and due date. Since January 2024, domestic and foreign for-profit and professional corporations file their annual report separately with the Secretary of State.

title: Alaska biennial report
finding: January 2 applies to business/professional corporations and LLCs, with even/odd formation-year parity. Nonprofit, cooperative and religious corporations have July 2 dates. Narrow the corporation scope.
originalDescription: Alaska corporations and LLCs file a biennial report every two years, due January 2. An entity formed in an even-numbered year files in even years; one formed in an odd-numbered year, in odd years. Filing opens three months before the due date, and reports filed after February 1 incur a late fee.

title: Arizona corporation annual report
finding: Commission FAQ confirms corporations file annually by their designated due date and LLCs do not file annual reports.
originalDescription: Arizona corporations file an annual report with the Arizona Corporation Commission each year by their designated due date. Arizona LLCs are not required to file an annual report.

title: Arkansas annual franchise tax report
finding: Official 2025 LLC franchise-tax form confirms May 1. The linked landing page does not substantiate every penalty/scope assertion. Qualify corporation coverage and confirm exemptions before seeding.
originalDescription: Corporations and LLCs registered in Arkansas file an annual franchise tax report and pay the tax to the Secretary of State by May 1. Late reports or payments incur penalties and interest.

title: California Statement of Information (LLCs)
finding: Secretary of State guidance confirms initial 90 days and biennial LLC filings. Clarify that subsequent statements can be filed during the six-month window ending with the anniversary month.
originalDescription: California LLCs file a Statement of Information within 90 days of registering, then every two years in the calendar month of their original registration. File an updated statement sooner if the information changes.

title: California Statement of Information (corporations)
finding: Secretary of State guidance confirms initial 90 days and annual stock/foreign-corporation filings. Clarify the six-month filing window; do not apply the annual cadence to nonprofit corporations.
originalDescription: California stock corporations and registered foreign corporations file a Statement of Information within 90 days of registering, then every year before the end of the calendar month of their original registration.

title: Colorado periodic report
finding: Annual periodic reports and the filing window extending two months after the report month are confirmed. Recheck the exact noncompliant/delinquent and late-fee wording before seeding.
originalDescription: Colorado corporations and LLCs file a periodic report every year. It is due by the last day of the second month after the entity's periodic report month, shown on its record with the Secretary of State — a January month means a March 31 deadline. A late report makes the entity noncompliant and adds a late fee.

title: Connecticut annual report
finding: The linked official page explains how to look up a deadline but does not establish the draft LLC/corporation date rules.
originalDescription: Connecticut LLCs file an annual report between January 1 and March 31 each year. Corporations and other business entities file on the anniversary of their formation or registration. All annual reports are filed online.

title: Delaware annual franchise tax
finding: March 1 is confirmed for Delaware domestic corporations. Foreign corporations have a different date. The LLC June 1 assertion needs the linked LLC/LP/GP tax source reviewed separately.
originalDescription: Delaware corporations file an annual report and pay franchise tax by March 1. Delaware LLCs file no report but pay a flat annual tax by June 1; missing it adds a $200 penalty plus monthly interest. This applies to entities formed in Delaware, wherever they operate.

title: District of Columbia biennial report
finding: Official FAQ confirms first April 1 after registration and then every two years. Exact late-fee/notice language remains to be checked.
originalDescription: Corporations and LLCs registered in DC file a biennial report — the first by April 1 of the year after registering, then by April 1 every two years. Reports filed after April 1 incur a late fee, and not receiving a reminder does not excuse a late filing.

title: Florida annual report
finding: Official annual-report URL was attempted; access was inconsistent/blocked. Do not attest the May 1 deadline or penalty until substantive source text is recovered.
originalDescription: Florida corporations and LLCs file an annual report between January 1 and May 1 each year. Profit corporations and LLCs that file after May 1 pay a $400 late fee.

title: Georgia annual registration
finding: Official guide confirms annual registration January 1–April 1 and advance multi-year filing. First-report timing and exact dissolution wording need final confirmation.
originalDescription: Georgia corporations and LLCs file an annual registration between January 1 and April 1, starting the year after formation. Registrations can be filed up to three years in advance. An LLC that does not file can be administratively dissolved.

title: Hawaii annual business report
finding: Original official URL redirects to the general Hawaii Business Express portal. Replace it with an authoritative page establishing the anniversary-quarter rule.
originalDescription: Hawaii corporations and LLCs file an annual business report each year during the calendar quarter in which they registered, by the last day of that quarter. Late reports incur a penalty for each year delinquent.

title: Idaho annual report
finding: Idaho statutory source timed out or was blocked. Anniversary-month and first-report assertions remain unverified.
originalDescription: Idaho corporations and LLCs file an annual report every year by the last day of the month in which they were formed or registered, starting the year after formation.

title: Illinois annual report
finding: Illinois official page was blocked on final retrieval. Verify separate domestic/foreign and LLC/corporation deadlines and penalty timing.
originalDescription: Illinois LLCs file an annual report before the first day of their anniversary month — the month they were organized. After 60 days late an LLC pays a $100 penalty, and one that stays delinquent is administratively dissolved. Corporations also file an annual report tied to their anniversary month, and may elect an extended filing month; the pre-filled report the Secretary of State sends shows the date.

title: Indiana business entity report
finding: Official INBiz guidance recovered through search confirms first report after two years and every other year thereafter, during the formation/registration anniversary month; the report becomes past due at month end.
originalDescription: Indiana corporations and LLCs file a business entity report every two years, by the end of the month in which they were formed. An entity formed in an even year files in even years; one formed in an odd year, in odd years. It is due even if the business is not operating.

title: Iowa biennial report
finding: Official help confirms LLCs file in odd years and profit corporations in even years. January–April filing window and August dissolution wording need an additional source.
originalDescription: Iowa LLCs file a biennial report in odd-numbered years, and for-profit corporations in even-numbered years, between January 1 and April 1. An entity that still has not filed by August is dissolved, or has its authority revoked if it is foreign.

title: Kansas information report
finding: Current official page specifies April 15 for for-profit entities and June 15 for nonprofits, every two years according to formation-year parity. Replace the draft fiscal-year/fourth-month formulation.
originalDescription: Since 2024, Kansas corporations and LLCs file an information report every two years instead of every year. A business formed in an even year files in even years; one formed in an odd year, in odd years. The month and day it is due did not change: the fifteenth day of the fourth month after the tax year ends — April 15 for a calendar year.
correctedDraftDescription: Kansas registered businesses file an information report every two years. Businesses formed in even-numbered years report in even years; those formed in odd-numbered years report in odd years. For-profit business reports are due April 15 and not-for-profit reports June 15. An entity that remains delinquent for three months after its due date may forfeit its registration.

title: Kentucky annual report
finding: Official annual-report and business-filing pages recovered through search confirm January 1–June 30 annual filing beginning the year after formation. Nonfiling can lead to domestic dissolution or foreign authority revocation.
originalDescription: Kentucky corporations and LLCs file an annual report between January 1 and June 30 each year. A Kentucky entity that misses June 30 is administratively dissolved until it reinstates.

title: Louisiana annual report
finding: Louisiana source returned no usable filing instructions. Find a current official anniversary-date source.
originalDescription: Louisiana corporations and LLCs file an annual report each year by the anniversary of their formation. The Secretary of State sends a renewal notice beforehand, and the report can only be filed close to that renewal date.

title: Maine annual report
finding: Maine source confirms annual June 1 filing. First-report timing, opening date and penalty/dissolution details remain unchecked.
originalDescription: Maine corporations and LLCs file an annual report between January 1 and June 1 each year, starting the year after formation. A late report incurs a penalty, and not paying it leads to administrative dissolution.

title: Maryland annual report
finding: Maryland source confirms April 15 beginning the year after formation. Confirm the annual-report/personal-property-return distinction and extensions before seeding.
originalDescription: Every corporation and LLC formed, qualified or registered in Maryland files an Annual Report (Form 1) with the Department of Assessments and Taxation by April 15, starting the year after formation. A business that owns or uses personal property in Maryland also files its personal property return on the same form. Not filing can forfeit the charter or the right to do business in Maryland.

title: Massachusetts annual report
finding: Massachusetts source distinguishes domestic LLC organization anniversary from foreign LLC Massachusetts registration anniversary. Corporations generally file within 2.5 months of fiscal-year end. Clarify the foreign LLC date.
originalDescription: Massachusetts LLCs file an annual report on or before the anniversary of their formation filing. Corporations file within two and a half months of their fiscal year end — around March 15 for a calendar year.

title: Michigan annual statement or report
finding: Michigan URL no longer yields substantive annual-report guidance. Confirm LLC February 15, September formation exception, corporation May 15 and whether the stated penalty applies only to PLLCs.
originalDescription: Michigan LLCs file an annual statement by February 15 each year; an LLC formed after September 30 skips the February immediately following. Corporations file an annual report by May 15. An LLC statement received after February 15 incurs a penalty.

title: Minnesota annual renewal
finding: Minnesota source confirms annual renewal by December 31 and reinstatement guidance. Recheck first-report timing and exact dissolution wording.
originalDescription: Minnesota corporations and LLCs file an annual renewal with the Secretary of State by December 31 each year, starting the year after formation. There is no fee for an entity in good standing, but one that does not renew is dissolved by statute.

title: Mississippi annual report
finding: Mississippi source gives January 1–April 15 for LLCs and for-profit corporations; nonprofits use May 15. Narrow the corporation scope.
originalDescription: Mississippi corporations and LLCs file an annual report online between January 1 and April 15 each year. A corporation that does not file is administratively dissolved.

title: Missouri annual registration report (corporations)
finding: Missouri source could not be fully substantiated. Check whether corporations may elect biennial reports and the legacy formation-date exceptions.
originalDescription: Missouri corporations file an annual registration report each year, due by the end of the month in which they incorporated or qualified. A corporation that existed before July 1, 2003 uses the month shown on its last report.

title: Montana annual report
finding: Montana linked help article now returns 404. Replace with current official guidance; do not retain unverified higher-cost late-filing wording.
originalDescription: Montana corporations and LLCs file an annual report between January 1 and April 15 each year. It renews the registration record rather than reporting earnings, and filing after April 15 costs more.

title: Nebraska biennial report
finding: Nebraska source confirms LLC reports in odd years due April 1 and business/professional corporation reports in even years due March 1. Nonprofit timing differs; qualify corporation scope and distinguish deadline from delinquency date.
originalDescription: Nebraska corporations file a biennial occupation tax report by March 1 of even-numbered years; LLCs file a biennial report by April 1 of odd-numbered years. Reports become delinquent after April 15 for corporations and June 16 for LLCs.

title: Nevada annual list and state business license
finding: Nevada source was blocked/embedded. Annual-list and business-license renewal deadlines remain unverified.
originalDescription: Nevada corporations and LLCs file an annual list of officers or managers and renew their state business license together, by the last day of the month in which they were formed. Filing late adds a penalty.

title: New Hampshire annual report
finding: New Hampshire official source returned 403. April 1 and associated scope/penalty statements remain unverified.
originalDescription: New Hampshire corporations and LLCs file an annual report by April 1 each year. Reports and fees received after April 1 incur a late fee.

title: New Jersey annual report
finding: New Jersey official source returned 403. Anniversary-month and revocation timing remain unverified.
originalDescription: New Jersey corporations and LLCs file an annual report every year by the last day of the month in which they were formed. The business is responsible even if no notice arrives, and not filing can lead to revocation.

title: New York biennial statement
finding: New York official guidance confirms biennial statements during the anniversary month, with no early filing.
originalDescription: New York corporations and LLCs file a biennial statement every two years, during the calendar month in which they were originally formed or authorized. It cannot be filed before that month.

title: North Carolina annual report
finding: North Carolina source confirms LLC April 15 and corporations the fifteenth day of the fourth fiscal-year month. Check first-report timing and exact scope before seeding.
originalDescription: North Carolina LLCs file an annual report by April 15 each year, starting the year after formation. Corporations file by the fifteenth day of the fourth month after their fiscal year ends — April 15 for a calendar year. A business that does not file can be administratively dissolved.

title: North Dakota annual report
finding: North Dakota distinguishes domestic business/professional corporations (August 1), foreign corporations (May 15), LLCs/PLLCs (November 15), and farming entities (April 15). Draft incorrectly assigns August 1 to all corporations.
originalDescription: North Dakota LLCs file an annual report by November 15 each year, and business corporations by August 1. A business that does not file loses good standing and can be involuntarily terminated if the report stays overdue for 6 to 12 months.
correctedDraftDescription: North Dakota annual reports first fall due in the year after registration. Domestic business and professional corporations generally report by August 1; foreign business and professional corporations by May 15; LLCs and professional LLCs by November 15. Farm, ranch and authorized livestock corporations and LLCs have an April 15 deadline. Confirm the entity classification and deadline shown by the Secretary of State.

title: Oklahoma LLC annual certificate
finding: Oklahoma source timed out. LLC anniversary filing and the separate franchise-tax termination claim need current official sources.
originalDescription: Oklahoma LLCs file an annual certificate each year on the anniversary of their formation, confirming the business is active and its principal address. (Oklahoma corporation franchise tax returns ended after tax year 2023.)

title: Oregon annual report
finding: Oregon official guidance confirms annual renewal on the registration anniversary and a renewal notice approximately 45 days beforehand.
originalDescription: Oregon corporations and LLCs renew with an annual report each year, due on the anniversary of their original filing. The Secretary of State sends a renewal notice about 45 days before.

title: Pennsylvania annual report
finding: Pennsylvania source confirms annual reports from 2025, corporation June 30 and LLC September 30 deadlines, and delayed administrative-dissolution enforcement beginning in 2027.
originalDescription: Since 2025 Pennsylvania requires an annual report from corporations and LLCs. Corporations file by June 30; LLCs file between January 1 and September 30. From reports due in 2027, an entity that does not file is dissolved or terminated six months after the due date.

title: Rhode Island annual report
finding: Rhode Island source confirms February 1–May 1 for LLC/business-corporation reports and late fees from June 1. Benefit-corporation reports are a separate obligation.
originalDescription: Rhode Island corporations and LLCs file an annual report between February 1 and May 1 each year, starting the year after registration. Filing late adds a fee.

title: South Carolina corporation annual report
finding: South Carolina corporate FAQ distinguishes C-corporation fourth-month and S-corporation third-month return dates. The draft applies the C-corporation date to all corporations. Confirm Schedule D annual-report scope in the replacement copy.
originalDescription: South Carolina corporations file an annual report (Schedule D) with the Department of Revenue alongside the corporate income tax return, by the same due date — April 15 for a calendar year. An LLC taxed as a corporation files it too; an LLC taxed as a partnership or disregarded entity does not.
correctedDraftDescription: South Carolina's corporate annual report is Schedule D of the applicable corporate income tax return. Filing obligations and due dates depend on the entity's tax classification and fiscal year; dormant corporations can still have filing obligations. LLCs not taxed as corporations and other specifically exempt entities are excluded. Check the Department of Revenue guidance for the applicable corporate return and license-fee requirements.

title: South Dakota annual report
finding: South Dakota source confirms the first day of the anniversary month and a two-month late period. Qualify late-fee scope because nonprofits are treated differently.
originalDescription: South Dakota corporations and LLCs file an annual report by the first day of their anniversary month each year — a company formed on June 11 files by June 1. Late fees start two months after the due date.

title: Tennessee annual report
finding: Tennessee source returned 403. Fourth-month/fiscal-year deadline and penalty details remain unverified.
originalDescription: Tennessee corporations and LLCs file an annual report by the first day of the fourth month after their fiscal year ends — April 1 for a calendar year.

title: Texas franchise tax and Public Information Report
finding: Texas May 15 annual deadline is confirmed, but entities below the no-tax-due threshold generally no longer file a No Tax Due Report for 2024 onward; applicable information reports remain. Veteran-owned and other exemptions need scope qualification.
originalDescription: Texas corporations and LLCs file an annual franchise tax report with the Comptroller by May 15, together with a Public Information Report or Ownership Information Report. Even an entity that owes no tax must file the information report, or it can forfeit its right to do business in Texas.
correctedDraftDescription: Texas annual franchise-tax obligations are generally due May 15, or the next business day when that falls on a weekend or holiday. For report years 2024 and later, entities at or below the applicable no-tax-due revenue threshold no longer file a No Tax Due Report, but generally still file a Public Information Report or Ownership Information Report. Special exemptions and entity-specific rules apply; confirm your report-year threshold, entity classification and required forms with the Comptroller.

title: Utah annual renewal
finding: Utah current page confirms annual renewal but does not state the draft anniversary deadline or grace-period details. Read the relevant entity-specific authority before seeding.
originalDescription: Utah corporations and LLCs renew with the Division of Corporations every year by the anniversary of their registration. The renewal window opens 60 days before, when a notice goes to the registered agent.

title: Vermont annual report
finding: Vermont official source returned 403. Verify separate LLC/corporation fiscal-year filing windows.
originalDescription: Vermont LLCs file an annual report within three months after the end of the fiscal year on record, and corporations within two and a half months.

title: Virginia annual report and registration fee
finding: Virginia statute confirms corporation annual reports in the anniversary month, with permitted filing-date changes. It does not substantiate the draft LLC registration-fee/cancellation claims; add separate statutory support.
originalDescription: Virginia corporations file an annual report with the State Corporation Commission by the last day of their anniversary month each year, and pay an annual registration fee by the same date; the report can be filed up to three months early. Virginia LLCs pay the annual registration fee by the last day of their anniversary month, and one that has not paid by the end of the third month after is automatically cancelled.

title: Washington annual report
finding: Washington official source shows month-end report deadlines and notice guidance. Confirm anniversary attribution and dissolution timing before seeding.
originalDescription: Washington corporations and LLCs file an annual report by the last day of their anniversary month each year. A business that misses it goes delinquent and can be administratively dissolved.

title: West Virginia annual report
finding: West Virginia official source gives June 30 as the deadline, with January 1–June 30 filing and the first report in the next year. Remove the draft July 1 deadline reference.
originalDescription: West Virginia corporations and LLCs file an annual report between January 1 and June 30 each year, starting the year after registration. Filing after the July 1 deadline adds a late fee.
correctedDraftDescription: West Virginia annual reports are filed between January 1 and June 30, beginning in the year after registration. Failure to file by June 30 may result in penalties, administrative dissolution or revocation. Confirm the report obligation for your registered entity with the Secretary of State.

title: Wisconsin annual report
finding: Wisconsin PDF was retrieved as binary but not successfully parsed in this review. Verify domestic versus foreign entity timing before treating the anniversary-quarter rule as universal.
originalDescription: Wisconsin corporations and LLCs file an annual report each year, during the calendar quarter that contains the anniversary of their formation, starting the year after formation.

title: Wyoming annual report and license tax
finding: Wyoming official source confirms annual filing on the first day of the anniversary month. The draft 60-day dissolution detail needs separate confirmation.
originalDescription: Wyoming corporations and LLCs file an annual report and pay license tax by the first day of their anniversary month — a company formed on May 15 files by May 1. An entity that has not paid within 60 days of the due date is subject to dissolution.

title: USDOT biennial update (Form MCS-150)
finding: FMCSA confirms biennial month/parity rules based on the USDOT digits. Add or account for the exception for an update in the preceding 12 months and distinguish changes that must be reported within 30 days.
originalDescription: Every entity with a USDOT number updates its registration with FMCSA every two years, even if nothing has changed. The last digit of the USDOT number sets the month; an odd next-to-last digit means odd-numbered years, an even one even years. Missing it deactivates the USDOT number and can bring civil penalties.

title: Unified Carrier Registration (UCR)
finding: FMCSA UCR landing page points to the UCR system but does not establish the annual registration window. Review current official UCR requirements directly.
originalDescription: Motor carriers, brokers, freight forwarders and leasing companies operating in interstate commerce register and pay UCR fees for each registration year, which runs with the calendar year. Registration for a year opens in the autumn before it, so register before operating in that year.

title: Heavy Highway Vehicle Use Tax (Form 2290)
finding: IRS source confirms the last day of the month after first use and August 31 for July first use, subject to non-business-day adjustments. Confirm taxable-weight scope and low-mileage tax-suspension exceptions.
originalDescription: If you operate a highway vehicle with a taxable gross weight of 55,000 pounds or more, file Form 2290 and pay the tax each year. For vehicles in use in July the return is due August 31; a vehicle first used later in the year is due by the last day of the month after its first use.

title: IFTA quarterly fuel tax return
finding: The linked IFTA carrier page does not establish the draft due-date wording. Standard quarterly deadlines are the last day of the following month, rather than freely chosen by each jurisdiction. Obtain current authoritative procedure/base-jurisdiction guidance before replacement and seeding.
originalDescription: If you run a qualified motor vehicle — two axles over 26,000 pounds, three or more axles, or a combination over 26,000 pounds — in two or more jurisdictions, you hold an IFTA license and file a quarterly fuel tax return with your base jurisdiction. It sends the return and rates each quarter and sets when they are due.

title: EPA Lead-Safe firm certification (RRP)
finding: EPA source confirms five-year firm certification and renewal at least 90 days before expiration. Clarify EPA versus authorized-state programs and covered pre-1978 work.
originalDescription: Firms, including sole proprietors, doing renovation, repair or painting in housing or child-occupied facilities built before 1978 must be EPA Lead-Safe certified. Certification lasts five years; apply to recertify at least 90 days before it expires to keep working without a gap.

title: DEA controlled substance registration
finding: DEA source permits continued authorized operations while a timely renewal application is pending. The draft absolute expiry statement omits that distinction. Verify the three-year practitioner category and renewal-window wording separately.
originalDescription: Practitioners who prescribe, administer or dispense controlled substances hold a DEA registration, renewed every three years online, no more than 60 days before it expires. Handling controlled substances under an expired registration is prohibited.

title: CLIA certificate
finding: CMS source confirms certificates and fees on a two-year cycle, with distinct New York/Washington processes. Clarify covered clinical testing and replace the redirected source URL.
originalDescription: A practice that tests human specimens — including only FDA-waived tests — needs a CLIA certificate. Every certificate type is effective for two years, and its fees are paid every two years to keep it.
